utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, kindly call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Today is Tuesday, 17th of November, 2009. Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom, the accused, the Defence counsel, the witness. Good afternoon to you, Mr. Kruger and Mr. Stringer and your case manager, and all the people assisting us. We're starting five minutes late for a reason that has nothing to do with the Trial Judges, who were in front of the door to the courtroom at 2.15. Mr. Registrar, you have three IC numbers for us, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 3D has submitted its objections to the Prosecution's request for admission of documents tendered through Witness Ivan Beneta. This list shall be given Exhibit IC1109. 4D has also submitted its objections to the Prosecution's request for submission of documents tendered through Witness Ivan Beneta. This list shall be given Exhibit IC1110. The Prosecution has also submitted its objections to 4D documents tendered through Witness Ivan Beneta. This list shall be given Exhibit IC1111. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'm going to read out an oral ruling on the Petkovic Defence's motion for leave to add Exhibit 4D01733 to its 65 ter list. In its motion of 9th November 2009, the Petkovic Defence asked the Trial Chamber for leave to add Exhibit 4D01733 to its 65 ter list. The Prosecution filed its response on the 10th of November, 2009, specifying that it did not object to the exhibit being added. The other parties did not express an opinion. The Trial Chamber first notes that the exhibit was submitted to Witness Milan Gorjanc at the hearing of 27th of October, 2009. However, the Petkovic Defence had not forewarned the Trial Chamber that the exhibit was not in its 65 ter list. Moreover, the Trial Chamber notes that the exhibit is tendered by the Petkovic Defence without prior notice of it being added to its 65 ter list. The Trial Chamber reminds all parties the provisions of Guide-Line 8 in the Trial Chamber's decision of the 24th of April, 2008; namely, that it falls to a party to first seek leave, before the appearance of the witness, if it intends to submit an exhibit that is not included in its 65 ter list, by way of written motion to the Trial Chamber, leave to add the said exhibit to the list. It must provide the reasons why this is essential to the case and the reasons why this exhibit was not on the list filed pursuant to Rule 65 ter (G) of the Rules. However, the Trial Chamber notes that this, Exhibit 4D01733, presents all the necessary indicia -- all the prima facie indicia of reliability, probative value, and relevance. Therefore, in spite of the lack of due diligence by the Petkovic Defence, and in the absence of any prejudice alleged by the other parties, the Trial Chamber decides to add the exhibit to the 65 ter list. Mr. Stringer, you have one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, and to everyone else. Just a technical matter for the record. Yesterday was the dead-line for the Prosecution to file its response to the Praljak Rule 89(C) document motion, and that response was filed or was sent to the Registry last night at around 6.00 p.m. However, we did not indicate in the e-mail that yesterday was the dead-line, and under the rules that the Registry operates under, the Registry treated the filing as having been made today, rather than yesterday. It's a technical matter. It's been distributed already to the parties, but I just wanted to bring it to the Trial Chamber's attention in the event that if it's an issue for any of the parties or the Trial Chamber, we can go back to Registry and have the filing changed so that it indicates correctly that it was filed or submitted on the 16th, which was the dead-line. But in any event, I just wanted to put that on the record in case it's an issue for any of the parties. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think it will be a problem at all. We're going to proceed with the cross-examination by the other Defence teams. 1D, Mr. Karnavas, do you have any questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. I do have questions and I will probably use up all of my time. However, it's my understanding that General Praljak will go first, then -- yes, General Praljak will go first. Then it will be the Coric team, and then I will go, assuming that there are no questions from the Pusic team, and I believe there may be some questions from the Stojic team. Of course, I can't speak for everybody, but that's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's start with the Praljak Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to you and everybody else in the courtroom. First of all, a technical point. We don't seem to have the transcript on our screens, and of course it's always useful to have it. Now, with your permission, the cross-examination will be conducted by General Praljak, himself, because it refers to part of the examination-in-chief by Ms. Alaburic relating to the siege of Mostar and the questions raised by Judge Antonetti towards the end of proceedings yesterday, once again linked to the siege of Mostar. Now, as we're dealing with military matters, and as we're dealing with the period when General Praljak was personally in the area himself, with your permission I'll cede the floor to General Praljak for him to conduct the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Pinter, how many minutes did you count on, because there are several different teams and you have altogether one hour and a half, so how many minutes are you going to need?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As the Defence has an hour and a half at its disposal, and since we have five Defence teams, all of which would like to conduct the cross-examination, that makes it 18 minutes apiece, if my arithmetic is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours and everybody else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Just give me a brief answer when you hear my question. Nika, would you hand out this, please? Oh, they've already been handed out. Fine, thank you. When you became commander of the 3rd Brigade of the Croatian Defence Council, did you ever, either alone at the level of the brigade, or at the level of the operative zone, or at the level of the Main Staff, and when I was the commander there, make any offensive plans towards the BH Army in the Mostar area?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, sir, I don't remember that the brigade took part in the elaboration of any operative offensive plans at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. So throughout that time, you were on the defensive or, rather, carrying out your defence assignments?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the brigade had exclusively defence assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: During that time from the 30th of June and later on in July, when you took over the brigade, and the coming months, the months after that, were you bombed with artillery weapons at your positions 'round the clock, day and night?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, every day. We were shelled every day by the artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Especially at night, could you know whether that artillery assault was coming from the Army of Republika Srpska or from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's something one cannot establish. You can't know that, because their artillery weapons - I'm talking about the BH Army - were in the vicinity of the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska, so we weren't able to distinguish where the shells, the projectiles, were coming from exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Colonel, do you know, especially with respect to the earlier period, that the Army of Republika Srpska - and this is something that Judge Antonetti asked you about - targeted both East Mostar and West Mostar, trying to bring about a conflict? Did you have any information about that? Were you aware of that? Did you discuss things like that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Army of Republika Srpska did target the positions in the area of Stolac right up until the date that you mentioned, that is to say, the 30th of June, and I can testify to that myself, directly, because as far as I can remember, several days before that particular date the projectiles launched from the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska led to three of my soldiers being killed in Stolac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you about Mostar, but did your brigade hold the positions south of Mostar, towards Blagaj?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my brigade did hold the positions from the town of Mostar to the Buna River.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Colonel, throughout that area did you see -- in front of you, were there houses in depth, family houses in that area? Was it a built-up area with family houses?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It was a built-up area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: And were those houses linked by road, with cars going along those roads?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: From your positions, could you see each of these roads between the houses, could you see the cars and the pedestrians moving around?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, especially not in Gnojnice, Dracevice. The roads were visible just in some places.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tell me, Colonel, did your brigade have its own artillery?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did, just like any other brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did you ever, you personally, give an order for some pedestrians to be targeted by the artillery, or did you receive an order to that effect from the Main Staff at any time during that period?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The artillery could target only military targets, pursuant to orders from a front-line commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you were a military commander yourself, at night how many people from Mostar, in your view, could go to Blagaj unimpeded and come back without anybody seeing them, and even if somebody wanted to shoot at them, they didn't know how, they couldn't see them? Men, women, children, how many using those roads in the area?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Gnojnice and Dracevice areas, you could move around that area at night without any major problems. You could even drive through. And on foot, you could go any time you liked and wouldn't be hindered. So maybe a thousand people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now, please, would you turn to P04103 -- no, I got it wrong. 4403. Yes, 4403. Take a look at this document quickly. I think you've already seen it. Do you know who the head, Branko Kvesic, is?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: What was he, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now, in this document, in the first part, it says that the Muslims -- that their people met representatives of the Army of Republika Srpska. At the time, did you have any information that was semi-public about these two armies holding meetings?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I said that yesterday. And with your permission, I've also remembered that I read a book by my friend, General Drekovic. He made me a present of the book, and in that book he says at one point -- or, rather, he describes the situation and says that after his arrival to the 4th Corps of the BH Army as commander, he found unmanned positions facing the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. We've already shown this book here in court. We've seen it. But tell me, during that summer and autumn of 1993, who attacked you, how many times, and with what intensity?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the summer of 1993, we were attacked by the BH Army, and that was two or three times, with greater intensity and with lesser intensity. The attacks were daily.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Colonel, in these offensive attacks, did they have any shortages in artillery pieces, or infantry, weapons, since, as the Prosecutor says, that they were under siege? Did they lack ammunition?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When they launched offensive actions in the Hum area, they had very strong artillery -- a very strong artillery. And judging by what they did up there and what we came across and found when we came across their dead, they were very well equipped.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Colonel, from this document do you know who, on the 30th of June, took control of all the hydroelectric power-stations from Mostar to Jablanica along the Neretva River? Who had control of them, in military terms?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The hydroelectric power-plants along the Neretva River from Jablanica to Mostar were controlled by the BH Army. I think four power-stations in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now look at the next document, which is 4D00798. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know who Sefer Halilovic was?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, on this document, which is an extensive one and I don't want to go through it all - all I'm interested in is "death to fascism, freedom to the Bosniaks" - how do you interpret this cry at the end of a text signed by the chief of the Main Staff of the BH Army, Sefer Halilovic? It says "death to fascism," so who are the fascists here, and what did the BH Army look like, if it says "freedom" and then "only to the Bosniaks"? What does that tell you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from this we can see that as far as he's concerned, everyone in Bosnia-Herzegovina was a fascist, they were all fascists, except for the Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now look at document 4D00793, which is the next document. Do you know who Arif Pasalic is?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now, this document is dated the 20th of September, 1993, and Arif Pasalic says here that the Ustashas are attacking the HVO and the HV, et cetera, et cetera. And then, in item 2, he goes on to say that: "Our forces," meaning the BH Army forces "have been moved towards the south, center, and north, and that they managed to take certain elevation points, important elevation points." Now, on the 20th of September, according to you, was that the fiercest attack within Neretva 93, precisely on the hill that you mentioned earlier on?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, General, sir, that is indeed the date when my unit, that is to say, the 3rd Brigade, suffered heavy losses when it lost control of part of its positions, when it was not prepared and ready for an action of that kind, because just a few days before a truce had been signed, and so they caught us unawares. We never thought that we could be -- that we could come under attack. So they took control of part of Hum Hill and part of the positions in town, as far as I remember, and also in the area of Kovacina and that general area down there. And we managed to regain control of it later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: And were all the positions regained later, the eastern ones?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: So is this a model of behaviour, that is to say, the HVO as Ustashas, the Croatian Army attacking the blameless BH Army, and then this is justification for their offensive actions? In your view, was that what -- the kind of thing we experienced down there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, sir, I said that I remember this date very well, and I can say with a great deal of certainty that at that time we respected the order for a truce and cease-fire that came in from several levels. And whenever a truce was agreed upon, there would be a BH Army attack launched against us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now, the next document is 4D00768. Do you know who Rasim Delic is?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's look at paragraph marked "3," which states that the staffs and commands of the 1st, 4th, and the 6th Corps must offer their assistance in the implementation of the assigned tasks. And it says "crossing from Dobrinja to Butmir." Is that Sarajevo, the exit from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say: "Transport on the direction from Igman to Mostar." "Transport," what does that mean, "transport from," when you leave Sarajevo from Igman to Mostar? When they say "transport," what do they mean; camels, donkeys, cars? Is it sitting in a car and going on a good road, or some part of it would be a macadam road and then we would reach Mostar?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What they mean is transport using motor vehicles, because there was a road along this direction. And I personally did go to Sarajevo via Igman, so that's how I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you look at 3D00567. 3D00567. Do you know where this Bijela Bridge is?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's north of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: And you know who Arif Pasalic is. Can you tell us what you can see from this document? We are talking about the Bijela Bridge, that it had been handed over to the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina for guarding; can we see that from this document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can read the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. It was supposed to be de-mined, the bridge?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: So who was on the bridge if the Bosnia-Herzegovina Army was supposed to de-mine it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosnia-Herzegovina Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you look at document 4D - it's the previous document - 00726. It's a document of the 26th of October, 1993. Who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Arif Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you please look at the document, Colonel, sir. Does it state that a unit of 20 soldiers would be assigned to --

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that will take up the positions at Kuci and Potok Bijela, Bijela Creek.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: But it says here "to strengthen" or "to fortify the lines." Who is on the bridge if 10 to 20 people are supposed to fortify the lines?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the strength of the force of that commander, so it would imply the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: All right, thank you very much. Let's look at the Bijela Bridge. We have three photographs, 3D03789. Let's look at the first one. That's 3D43-1383. Colonel, sir, could you please show us where the Bijela Bridge is or where the settlement that we call "Bijela" is? And can we give something to the witness so he can mark it? Can you please circle that spot and mark it with a "1"?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you please now indicate whether you see this lake on the Neretva? Can you show us where the dam is? Where does the lake end? Where is the lake or the reservoir, and where is the hydroelectric power-plant? Can you mark that with a number "2"?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can we look at the next photograph, 3D -- and you can initial the bottom of that photograph and the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, it might be good at this point for General Praljak to ask whether the conditions are exactly the same then as they are depicted in this particular photograph, because I believe it's out of Google, which is of today. So perhaps the gentleman would know. That way, there's no misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will see that better when we enlarge that place. So the Colonel can then say whether the situation is different now as compared to then. And let us look at the third photograph, finally, and then the witness can respond to Mr. Karnavas' question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, could you please answer the question put to us by Mr. Karnavas? He wanted to know whether the Google map that we have here, which dates 2009, reflects the same thing as existed in 1993, whether the town of Bijela was there, whether the river was there, whether the hydroelectric power-plant under number 2 is there also. So is it the same now as it was at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He says, "Of course." Very well. Registrar, could we have a number for the map?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The marked portion of 3D03789 shall be given Exhibit IC1112. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, please resume.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next map is 3D43-1384, and this is now enlarged so we can see better.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Colonel, these roads here around this area here, the Bay of Bijela, did they exist at the time when you were working in Mostar for two years, when the roads were constructed, they were being constructed then? Can you please show us those roads, and can you answer whether those roads existed then, and were they the same as we see on this map now?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. The roads did exist to the right of Bijela.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Yes, we'll see that on the next map. If you can just mark that with number 1, number 2, and number 3. And can we have a number for this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, could you please place figures 1, 2, and 3, since we have three roads?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can we have an IC number for this map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The second marked portion of document 3D3789 shall be given Exhibit IC1113. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: A small question, just to clarify that I interpret the map correctly. The road passing by Ravni looks here as if it were a dead-end road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It does not end in a dead-end. I cannot really tell here, specifically, but I think that it connects on to this road [indicates].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You think so, you think so. Do you see that on the map? Because I fail, really, to see it on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You cannot see it on the map, but there was a road in this area that you could reach on foot or pass on foot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Not a road, then, but a foot-path?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think -- I never passed that way, but as far as I know, I think that there was a road that you could use. You could pass -- you could perhaps not pass the road in a vehicle, but you could use other means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: What other means, except on foot and perhaps with a mule, do you have in mind; a motorcycle, a bicycle, a mountain bike?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In terrain like this, we were using horses, donkeys. These were the means that we used for transporting cargoes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honours, in my reluctant capacity as a sort of self-appointed map monitor, could I observe that at line 7 at page 16, "indicates," he indicated but didn't mark, and then when we get a few lines later on, "but there was a road in this area that you could reach on foot," all we got is "this area." And although at the time we could see on the map what he was talking about, nobody, in a few weeks or months' time, will know that. The maps really do need -- I have said it quite a few times now, with respect, Your Honour. Maps need very careful marking as we go along if any of us are going to be able to make proper use of them on the transcript in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, you drew three roads, 1, 2 and 3, in red. My fellow Judge asked you whether you could drive in a vehicle through these roads, and you said, No, these are just paths or trails. So could you please tell us, so that it's on the transcript, whether roads 1, 2, or 3 were asphalted roads on which vehicles could drive or whether these were earth trails where you could only move with mules, or animals, or motorbikes, but not with cars? Please make this specific so we know exactly how it was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You could drive in vehicles in a certain part, and then another part it was not possible to go in a vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could you tell us on which part vehicles could drive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This part from Bijelo Polje via Ravni-Jasenjani. These were villages that had been inhabited up until the war, people living there. They had their vehicles, and they would drive to their homes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Colonel, sir, do you know where Jasenjani is on this main road? Can you tell where Jasenjani is? If you don't know, you don't know.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it here, but it should be near Ravni.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: To the north or to the south?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ravni-Jasenjani, it should be to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRALJAK
utterances.text: Is it true or is it correct that you actually don't know whether you could pass in a vehicle and -- at the exact route? I mean, do you know this exactly or perhaps you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to the village of Ravni-Jasenjani, you could go by vehicle. I know that 100 per cent. As for the rest of that road, I don't know what the road is like because I was never there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Let's look at the third map, 4D31385.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise for interrupting General Praljak, but if I may perhaps again take up the point that my learned colleague Mr. Stewart has made. After the witness signed the IC Exhibit 1113, after that time he made another marking, Your Honour, and that is from just left of the name "Gomile" or "Gomite," and that's the line which then proceeds for about 10 centimetres. And if he could perhaps just explain what that marking is that he made, and perhaps mark that as well as a number 4, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, when you started to draw these four roads, 1, 2 and 3, road number 3 stopped at one point in time, and my fellow Judge asked you whether this road was a dead-end. You said, No, and then you drew a line to join it with road number 2. And I see that you have actually marked number 4 on this portion of road. So could you tell us what exactly this number 4 means so it's on the transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 4 marks that section that I'm not sure you could pass in a motor vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's on the transcript. Number 4 marks the section where the witness is not sure that a motor vehicle could pass. General Praljak, you have the floor. General Praljak, you have already run over your time by 7 minutes. Our Registrar is telling us that you've already used 25 minutes. So please finish your cross-examination, and of course this time will be deducted from the time allotted to other teams. The Registrar is also telling me that this map needs an IC number. Registrar, could we have an IC number for this new map?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not going to stand here and have my time deducted because another Defence had to do their questioning. Otherwise, if that is the new rule, then I will be objecting as soon as -- I'll keep my own time and then start objecting and cutting off witnesses or cutting off my colleagues. But I don't think that we can just subtract. It's not fair to the rest of us. The rest of us have cases. We're not monolithic here. I keep saying this over and over again. But Mr. Praljak does need to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're absolutely right, Mr. Karnavas, as usual. But the Registrar -- Mr. Registrar, please give us a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The third marked portion of document 3D03789 shall be given Exhibit IC1114. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak, you have spent 7 minutes -- you've run your time -- you've run over by 7 minutes. You know, and Mr. Karnavas doesn't want to give you any time. I don't know if others want to give you any time. Maybe Mr. Pusic's Defence can give you some time. I don't know where you stand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I'm not going to burden anyone. Colonel, sir, thank you very much for responding to my questions. I'm sorry that I couldn't put a couple of more questions to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, we understood that you're not very familiar with the roads that you drew on the map. It looks like these were earth trails, but I'm a bit surprised. Can't a car or a vehicle go through an earth trail? A long time ago, you know, I remember in Arizona, in the US, there were earth trails on Indian reservations, and I was driving on these earth trails. Of course, this is not Arizona, but is it totally impossible to drive a car through these earth trails?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You could not drive a car along some roads, but you can drive a car along a macadam road that is in a better condition, and we did drive along the macadam roads, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Coric's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, and everybody else in the courtroom. I'd like to ask for the usher's assistance. Could he come up to collect some documents to hand out? The documents have been handed 'round to the interpreters, so these are documents for the Prosecution, the Trial Chamber, and the witness. Your Honours, I hope I'll be able to get through everything I had planned to do in 18 minutes. However, if that time is not sufficient, I'm going to ask permission from the Trial Chamber to allow me, as it allowed me in Mr. Buntic's case, with the 1D witness and with the 3D witness of General Praljak, to use the time allotted to the Coric Defence. So it might just be 10 or 15 more minutes. There was a previous decision to that effect. If I may use the overall time and take some minutes from the overall time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please try and make it in 18 minutes. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: My name is Ms. Tomasegovic Tomic, and as you've just heard, I shall be conducting the cross-examination on behalf of the Coric Defence. You have the documents in front of you, and I'll take them in the order that you have them before you. And the first document that I'd like us to look at is 5D0344 -- 5D03044. Have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Is this one of your orders, dated the 14th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: In the order, it says that it is pursuant to the order of the commander of the 1st Brigade, and this particular order relates to the introduction of a police curfew and putting that curfew into effect. And we see that the order was sent to the Stolac military police, the police station in Stolac, and all the units, et cetera, et cetera, not having to go through them all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, Mr. Pavlovic, according to the establishment of the military police in the Stolac area, we had the 3rd Stolac Platoon, the 3rd Company and the 3rd Military Police Battalion; am I right? They were active in the area?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: So we can conclude, then, when you say "the military police of Stolac," you actually mean that particular platoon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on to the next document, which is document number P01888. This is an order, again, dated April, from the commander of the Operative Zone for South-East Herzegovina, Miljenko Lasic, but Petar Zelenika signed for him, for the commander. Tell me now, please, you belonged to the South-East Herzegovina Operations Zone, did you not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: So underneath the date, we see that the order follows on from an order issued by the Main Staff, and in item 1 we see that it relates to the organisation of an operation. I don't have to read everything. You can see it for yourself. In point 2, we have the forces listed to take part in the operation, and a military police squad from the 3rd Military Police Battalion. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Then in item 5, it says that the commander-in-chief for all the forces is the commander of the 2nd Brigade. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: And at the bottom, we see that the order was sent to, among others, the 3rd Military Police Battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Pavlovic, according to the establishment of the military police in the Operative Zone of South-Eastern Herzegovina, we had the 3rd Military Police Battalion active there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next document, then, please, which is 5D03046. This is another order of yours, once again dated April, and it relates to letting through people through check-points, disarming anybody who goes against orders, and at the bottom we see that it was sent to the military police and the police station; is that right? Do you recognise this order?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: So we're dealing with the same military police unit that we mentioned earlier on, it's always that same unit; right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Now, just look at the number at the top of the order. The last digits are 93-515 [as interpreted]. And now we come to 5D03048, which is the next document I'd like us to look at. Here we have an approval from you. It doesn't say "Order," "I hereby order." It says: "I hereby approve." Just let me take a moment, please. The document that we're looking at now is 5D03048, for the record. As I said, this is an approval from you sent to the same military police unit and the police station, and it is one of your documents; right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: And in the last sentence, it refers to an order from the previous document. You can check that out by looking at the numbers, 5D03046 was the number of the document, of the previous document; is that right? Can you compare those numbers and tell us?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next document now, please, which is 5D03052, and -- yes, I said 5D03052. This is another order of yours once again sent to the military police of Stolac, and this time to the Command of the 4th Battalion. Do you recognise this order as being one of yours?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next document, which is P0 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General -- Colonel, I mean, when you sent this type of order to the military police, does this mean that you are telling them that you have authority over them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In part, yes, because they were attached to the unit to perform police assignments in that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You're saying, Yes, in part. Well, could you tell us in which area you do not have authority over them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't supervise them. That is, I can't order them to go into combat, for example, and I can't order them to do other things, either. I can't remember all the instances. But as far as police assignments, like setting up check-points, taking people into custody, and things like that, then they were at the disposal of the unit on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are saying that you couldn't order them to go into combat, but if the unit of the military police is subordinated to your brigade, in that case can you give them order -- can you order them to go into combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it was attached for police purposes, for carrying out police assignments, then I can issue them assignments from their police activities. However, if there is permission from a superior, then I can attach them to a unit engaged in combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, well, your answer is rather vague, not very specific, but I'm trying to understand what you're saying. If the order comes from a higher officer, for instance, the commander of an operational group, then you can send them into combat and you have authority over them; is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not have any such occasion. However, if my superior issues an order to me, telling me that I can send them into combat, then I can do that, because probably he had agreed upon something like that previously.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Not so relevant question, but could you tell us where this place or locality or area, Begovina settlement, is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is located at the exit to Stolac town, towards Berkovici, and it's up at the front-line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, to avoid any misunderstandings, in your response to the questions linked to command of the military police, you are speaking as a battalion commander and your experience in that post, how you functioned in the Stolac area; am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next document, which is P01913.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Mindua has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Excuse me, Ms. Tomasegovic. I just want to be sure I understood the witness's answer properly, when he spoke about orders to be issued to the military police, the Battalion of the Military Police. Witness, Witness Pavlovic, you said that you could, in part, give orders to military police within your battalion if you, yourself, had received instructions from your superior. Could you tell us from at what level of authority this superior should be and whether he, himself, must have or has authority over the military police? Because military police is separate from other fighting units. You see, what I fear is this: For instance, your superior, giving you instructions to send men from the military police to the front-line, would not have the authority to issue such an order. What do you think of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only carry out the orders I receive from my immediate superior, in this case the commander of the 1st Brigade. Now, probably -- well, who he decides this with, I don't know. But if he has reached a decision and has reached an agreement and gives me an order, then I will carry it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move on to P01913, the next document I'd like us to look at.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: This is titled a "Request" by your superior, Colonel Nedjeljko Obradovic, and he says that entry to certain persons should not be allowed, that others should be detained for 15 days, and so on. We see that the request was sent to the active service military police. Now, would you look at the number up at the top and remember it? Keep that number, because we'll come back to it, but tell me, have you ever seen this request before?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Let's move on to the next document, which is P01972. And this is a daily report from the Command of the 3rd Battalion -- 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion of the Military Police of Capljina. According to the establishment, the 3rd Company of 3rd Battalion was active in the Capljina area; am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Now take a look at what it says under the heading of "Security," incidents of security interest. It says there that: "Acting upon order number," and then you have the number, "1100-01-93-236," "another two people have been taken into custody and detained at the Grabovina barracks for 15 days." Would you look at the number there and tell us whether it is the number in the previous document, P01913 being the number of the previous document?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have an objection to how counsel called the previous document, which is a request, not an order. I think she misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, when I spoke earlier on, I said "Request," it is titled, but in the report it is referred to as "Order."

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But then it might not be the same document, because a request is a request, and an order is an order.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely why I'm reading out the number of the document. So it was in P01913. I'll read the number there again. It is 1100-01-01-93-236. Now let's look at the number in the report under the title "Incidents of Security Interest," which is 1100-01-93-236.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the numbers aren't the same, because in the second document it's "01" just once. In the previous document, it was "01-01"; that is to say, "01" came twice.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go back to the contents of the document, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Put your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go back to the request, and let's see what the request asks, what Mr. Obradovic asks in his request. He says, under item 1: "The entry of BH Army members is not allowed into our area of responsibility from Rotimlje to Drenovac without my written clearance." And then in item 2, he says: "All members of the BH Army carrying BH Army insignia are to be arrested immediately and detained for 15 days." Now, in P01972, the other document, and the signatory is Mr. Ancic, the commander of the 3rd Company of the 3rd Battalion, says that: "Acting on the order, another two people have been taken into custody and placed in detention in the Grabovina barracks for a period of 15 days." Witness, I'm now going to put a question to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: In view of the text that I have just read, is this an identical request to the order that was made in Mr. Ancic's report? If you're unable to answer, please say so. And if you are able to, can you please tell me if you know about it and if this was implemented?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a little bit confusing, but I think it is the same request.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Can we look at the next document. This is 5D02195. This is an order for taking into custody issued by commander of the 3rd Battalion of the 3rd Company of the Military Police. In the order, the commander is again referring to an order, and it has the same number as the one in the report. But the only difference is the "1100-01" number from the request by Mr. Obradovic. But since we're talking about an order to take into custody, I conclude that again we're talking about the implementation of the same request. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: You have to speak up, sir. We didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Pavlovic, can you please tell us why you think that -- or do you know why the persons who signed the report and the order refer to this request by Mr. Obradovic as a order? Do they believe that they have to act upon it in the same way as if it was entitled an order? As it is a request, do they have the same weight?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can recall from my testimony yesterday, I noticed a document that is identical to this request, but it is in the form of an order. Perhaps that's where the confusion lies.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Sir, let's move to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may just add a small question. I see on this list one Edo Obradovic. It seems to me that you have spoken about one Edo Obradovic yesterday. Is it the same person? Can you say anything about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's possible that it's the same person. But from what I can remember, we had several people with the name Edin Obradovic in my unit, nicknamed Edo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to move to the next document. This is 5D04380. This is another order sent to the same unit of the military police in Stolac from late April 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document. This is 5D03019. This is an order by Colonel Obradovic. I don't think that it's his signature. I think somebody signed the document for him, but I cannot tell who it was. It's an order from late May 1993, and it states that: "With the actions of the 1st HVO Brigade VOS information on activities and intentions of the B and H Army units and members, and with a view to more efficient co-ordination and operation of the units providing security in depth of the 1st HVO Brigade Knez Domagoj, issues the following order:" And then under number 1, Mr. Obradovic commands the military police Active Service Company to provide security at check-point passes. And then somewhere in the middle of that paragraph, it refers to the Stolac check-point, with two military policemen. Then in paragraph 2, the MUP Capljina police station is tasked. And then the third paragraph refers to the assignment for the Stolac MUP police station, and so on. Then in item 9, it says that civilian police, active service, and home guard commanders are responsible for the implementation of the order. And we see that the order is addressed precisely to those persons. Can you please tell me, Mr. Pavlovic, if you are familiar with this order? Was there a Gorica-Stolac check-point that is referred to here?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Check-points changed from day to day as needed. When it was necessary, we did maintain a check-point for a long time. This is the check-point at Aladinici, and the other check-points were set up as needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this order? Did you see it before? Did you know that actions and operations were co-ordinated in this way?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see -- I cannot recall seeing the order, but that's probably how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document. This is 5D0 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have two minutes left to finish.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to just skip some things, then. Your Honours, it's important to me to show the period. I have several documents, and I asked at the beginning, and I'm asking again, if I may spend a few minutes allocated to Mr. Coric's Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Coric. Before you take the floor, I want to state my own feeling. This witness is appearing on behalf of the Petkovic Defence to speak to the events in Stolac, to the problems with the Serbs. Your lawyer is now tackling from an angle that was not at all mentioned in the examination-in-chief, which is the issue of the military police. You will have an opportunity to call your own witnesses on this topic. Therefore, if you're given additional time, this creates a total imbalance, when it comes to witnesses called to speak to a specific topic, to address the points of view of all and the accused. So this being said, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yesterday, during the examination-in-chief, this witness was invited to testify that the military police was under the command of someone else and not the people who we are talking about today in our cross-examination, and it is very important to us, this topic. We very rarely request additional time, and today we insist that we be given more time in order to complete our cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honours, if you permit me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. After discussing the issue on account of Mr. Coric's intervention, who said that this was really exceptional for him to ask additional time, the Trial Chamber grants the Coric Defence 15 additional minutes that will be taken out of his overall time. In other words, you have another 15 minutes to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you permit me, I'm not going to oppose this decision. To the contrary, I wanted to support the request by my colleague for extra time. I would just like to clarify one thing. In the examination-in-chief, the military police was referred to exclusively in the context of the rights of the chief of the Main Staff to command the military police. The topic of our examination-in-chief was not what was happening with the military police in certain areas of Herceg-Bosna. I absolutely appreciate the interest of Mr. Coric and additional time for their cross-examination, and I support that, but at the same time I would also like it to be taken into account that this really is a new aspect of a topic. So during my redirect, I would like to be permitted some extra time in order to be able to cover this topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, let us now look at 5D01054. This is also your order sent to the SSD and the military police. Do you recognise this order? This is from May 1993.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document. This is 502548 [as interpreted]. This is a document -- P02548, and it is a command by the commander of the 1st Brigade sent to, among others, to the military police of Stolac and the active forces in Dretelj. These units are in the area of responsibility of Mr. Obradovic. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which units are you thinking of? I am reading the document, so I wasn't following.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: I apologise to you. I was perhaps a bit fast. It's the military police in Stolac and the active police in Dretelj. They're also in the area of responsibility of Colonel Obradovic. One is in Capljina, and the other one is in Stolac. The brigade covers Capljina and Stolac? This is my question.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document. This is P02640. This is a search warrant that you sent to the Stolac military police in June 1993. Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document. This is P03135. And while we're looking for the document, I am just going to put one question to you. Based on the documents that we've looked at so far, it's clear that before the 30th of June, 1993, you and the commander of the 1st Brigade were issuing orders to the military police in your area of responsibility; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was issuing orders to them for the police assignments in my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Now we have the document P03135. This is an order also by Colonel Obradovic on the 3rd of July, 1993. I'm going to read just the preamble and paragraph 1, because they're important to us. And it states in the document: "Based on the newly-arisen situation in the zone of responsibility of the Knez Domagoj 1st Brigade of the HVO, and due to increased crime and irresponsible behaviour by some commanders and soldiers of the HVO 1st Brigade, and pursuant to unlimited powers conferred on me over civilian and military structures in accordance with the broadening of the area of responsibility, I hereby order:" And then in paragraph 1, it states: "Prevent any theft or any other form of appropriation of personal and other property of people in our zone of responsibility. Arrest the perpetrators and institute criminal proceedings against them through this command." Before I put my question in relation to this document, I would like you to look at document 5D04392. This is your order of the same date, the 3rd of July, where you say: "Pursuant to the order of the commander of the HVO 1st Knez Domagoj Brigade, I hereby order: "Members of the military police, personnel of the civilian police, and those other soldiers assisting in manning check-point posts in the IZM Stolac zone of responsibility are to prevent the theft of all movable property," and then that type of property is listed, as well as weapons and military equipment. The order was sent to the military and to the civilian police. Mr. Pavlovic, can you please tell me whether you recognise this order and whether the order by the commander of the 1st Brigade, to which you refer, is actually the one that we looked at in document P03135?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: I'm going to look at two more documents, and we will be finished in a few seconds. Let's look at document P03019. It's a document that was shown to you by Mr. Petkovic's Defence yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel, I have a question for you. I've just had a look, a more thorough look at your order of the 3rd of July, 1993. At the end of the day, you're asking for Colonel Obradovic's order to be carried out. But regardless of the fact that you were given an order, I'd like to know this: The commander of a unit, can he, without having received any prior order, ask the military police to arrest and seize the weapons of individuals who are not supposed to carry those weapons or move about? Is that not a classical task of a military police at check-points, to carry out controls, and when they find somebody with a weapon that is not authorised, that person is arrested and the weapon is taken? Do you really need an order to do that sort of a job?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said that the police in the zone carried out military police assignments pursuant to our orders, and that is precisely the job they should do; that is to say, to control the area. And anything else, if there's any crime or anything like that, then they have to prevent that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By way of an example, your order was sent to the civilian police. Very well. Among the classical task of a civilian police, they have to combat trafficking with food in wartimes, all the people who sell food at very high prices. All that sort of offences is the responsibility of the civilian police. They don't need orders by the military police to do that sort of work. Why do you give an order to the civilian police? Because it's part -- by law, part of their job to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right, but perhaps at that point in time they didn't have all the necessary information about what was going on there, and then we had to co-operate with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me give you another example. Let's take a civilian. Normally, he should not be carrying a weapon, unless he has a hunting rifle and also he has a permit to have it. But apart from that situation, he's not supposed to have a weapon. When a civilian policeman sees a civilian with a military weapon, well, he can arrest that person without having an order to do so; do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would like to add a question referring to even a more previous document, P03135, but I don't think you have to look it up because it's a very small thing. Here, Colonel Obradovic speaks of "unlimited powers conferred on me over civilian and military structures." What is your comment to this? Is that a correct description of the legal situation or is Colonel Obradovic going a bit beyond what the correct description of his position would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see here for the first time that Colonel Obradovic sent an order of this kind, and I really don't know what the motive was. Perhaps somebody prepared that order for him and he just happened to sign it without really looking at it properly. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Try to finish before the break. It would be good for you to finish and for us to finish with you before the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pavlovic, let's look at document P03019, which is a document shown to you by the 4D Defence yesterday. And I'd like us to focus on item 10 of that document. During my cross-examination, we have seen orders which you, yourself, sent to the military police of Stolac throughout the spring, including the beginning of July, 1993, and they were sent in the same way every time. And if I understood you correctly, in response to a question, I think, by the Presiding Judge, you said that you knew what was going on from your level of command downwards and that you acted according to the orders given to you by your superior, immediate superior officer, in this case Mr. Obradovic. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Am I also right in concluding that you, in fact, have no knowledge about what was going on about your command level and in what way the orders were sent and reached Colonel Obradovic? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise to object at this late stage, but I think for such a crucial point and this being a new topic, it's not appropriate that this information is solicited by leading questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is not a new topic, because the witness, on transcript page 46843 to 46845, was asked what the authorisations were of the chief of the Main Staff linked to command over the military police, and I just want to clear up with the witness what level -- what his knowledge was, to ask him whether he knew what was going on on the ground, whereas that he didn't know about other things and couldn't testify about them. So I'd like the witness to tell me whether I'm right or wrong when I say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I agree with what you've said, but I find your question not clear. You say: "He had no knowledge about what was going on about your command level."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Above," interpreter's correction, "above."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I suspected that there was a problem with the translation, and it's now been set straight. Please go on. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, it's been corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer to my last question? Am I right or not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Well, then give me one now.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please? But make it shorter, because it was rather a long one.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: From your testimony here today, I concluded, on the basis of your answers to me and your responses to the Trial Chamber's questions, that you base your answers on your knowledge emanating from your experience. And your experience was how you commanded those you were in a position to command in the area in which you were active in, and the orders that you received from your immediate superior, which was Mr. Obradovic. Am I right there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Then I can conclude that you don't have direct knowledge, and you've already told the Presiding Judge that in your response, what was happening above that level; that is to say, from whom and in which way orders reached Colonel Obradovic, himself?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: So now in the document that we have before us, let's look at item 10. In item 10, in brackets, it says: "Co-operate with all forces in your zone." And then it says: "ATG," anti-terrorist groups, "the police, and military police outside your structure." Now, in view of the orders that I showed you here today, can you tell me and do you know which was this military police outside your structure and whether it was conveyed to you in that way? Because as far as I understood it yesterday, you didn't see the order in written form, but you received part of that order orally from Mr. Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection to those orders, because Mr. Obradovic didn't say that he received the order from General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: You said that some of these contents you received orally from Mr. Obradovic; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Now, did Mr. Obradovic mention the military police outside your structure at all?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember. It was 17 years ago, after all. I can just remember the assignment I was given in general terms, but not the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what this means, "military police outside your structure"? What is that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we are to interpret the definition, then it is a unit which is outside the unit which somebody commands.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: So that would be some other military police unit coming into the zone, not the one that you commanded, that is to say, the platoon from Stolac; is that how I'm to understand it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Now let's move on to the next document, Mr. Pavlovic, which is P03160. It is the last document, and I'll be finished in a moment. It is an order from Colonel Nedjeljko Obradovic, commander of Sector South, dated July 1993, in which he says that: "Due to the current situation in the field, and in order to protect the citizens and towns, as well as their property, I hereby issue the following order:" Item 1: "The security protecting of the citizens of the towns of Capljina and Stolac shall be taken over by the civilian police of Capljina and Stolac in order to prevent looting and violence." Item 2: "I hold the commanders of the civilian police of Capljina and Stolac responsible for the execution of this order." "Delivered to" at the bottom, it says: "The commander of the civilian police of Capljina." And: "The commander of the civilian police of Stolac." Tell me now, Mr. Pavlovic, whether you've ever seen this order before or did you know about it? And that's my last question.

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see this order at that time, because it's the day that I left Stolac and I can't remember having seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Pavlovic. Thank you, Your Honours. That completes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We're going to break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And, again, good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. And good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I just have four brief matters, and I think we can get through them rather quickly. If I can have you look at first at 1D01704. You have it in front of you, and if you could look at that very quickly. And then if you could also take a moment to also look at 4D01067. They're both connected, and my questions will --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Into the microphone, please, Counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My questions will relate to these two documents on the first topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before, sir?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw this second document during the proofing session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as I understand it, during this period of time, if we look at the documents, they seem to be -- the first one, that is, 1D01704, on or about 18 September 1993, and the other document, 4D01067, is 19 September 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second one, yes. But as to the first one, I can't read the date. I assume it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, this would have been the period when you were at the Heliodrom; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I just want to just briefly touch upon a couple of things. We can see on the first document, 1D01704, the preamble, we see that -- that this is pursuant to Article 30, and it says: "... as the supreme commander of the armed forces ..." And if we go to items, for instance, 3, there is an order that says: "The conditions in detention centres for prisoners of war which are not in keeping with those envisaged in the International Law of War and the Geneva Convention shall immediately be rectified accordingly. The prisoners of war shall be treated in compliance with the Geneva Convention provisions and other humanitarian norms." And of course if we look all the way down, we see this is signed by Mate Boban; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if we look at paragraph number 7, we see that: "The Main Staff of the HVO shall communicate this order to all subordinated commands and units, and render professional assistance in its implementation." My first question to you regarding this particular paragraph is: At this point in time, who is your immediate superior officer?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brigadier Miljenko Lasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we could turn to 4D01067, 4D01067, the next document, dated 19 September 1993, we see that it's an order, and would you agree with me that this is signed by -- it is signed for Mr. Lasic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And, of course, we see that this order is copied to various units or sectors; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And immediately after that, we also see something that is attached to this particular order, and that is from the Office of the President, dated 15 September 1993. And if we look at the next page, we see -- or if we look at the bottom of this document, we see that it's signed by Mate Boban; correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if we look at this attachment and we look at number 3, again it says: "Immediately ensure all conditions in case that they have not been provided in the detention centres for prisoners of war, and ensure that they are stipulated by the International Military Law and the Geneva Convention. Observe provisions of the Geneva Convention as well as other humanitarian standards during treatment of prisoners of war." And then if we look at number 7: "The HVO Main Staff will inform all subordinated commands and units with this order, and offer expert assistance in realisation of the aforementioned." Having looked at this second document, 4D01067, would it not appear that Mr. Lasic is acting pursuant to the order that was issued by President Boban?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this would have been a period when, at least as you've indicated, the second document would have been sent to you or you would have been informed of it from your immediate commander, Miljenko Lasic; correct? And that's my last question for this?

utterances.speaker: BOZO PAVLOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's move on to another subject. Yesterday, you were referenced to a statement by someone, and the document is P10153. That should be in the binder that was provided to you by the Petkovic Defence. Do you have that available at the moment? Mr. Usher, could you see to it that the gentleman has P10153 from yesterday.
